learning_outcomes.text: Will know the kinematics and dynamics of mechanical systems and will be able to apply the composition of movements to the kinematic analysis of machines.
Will know the parameters used in mass geometry and will be able to apply them in the calculation of geometric parameters specific to beams in two-dimensional sections.
Will understand and be able to apply the gyroscopic effect to vehicles.
Will understand the statics of mechanical systems and be able to apply it to the calculation of forces in machines and statically determined bar structures.
Will understand and be able to apply the equations of funicular solids statics for cable calculation.
Will understand and be able to apply the dynamics of impacts and collisions.
Will understand and be able to apply the phenomenon of mechanical vibrations in mechanical systems with one degree of freedom.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Magnitudes and units. Dimensional equations. Scalar and vector magnitudes. Vector calculus.
Kinematics. Kinematic magnitudes. Curvilinear motion. Tangential and normal accelerations. Rectilinear motion. Parabolic motion. Circular motion. Simple harmonic vibratory motion. Relative movements.

Particle Dynamics. Newton's Laws. Universal law of gravitation. Weight. Friction forces between surfaces. Dynamics of mechanical systems with vibratory motion. Dynamics in accelerated reference frames. Inertial forces. Kinetic energy. Work. Power. Conservative forces and potential energy. Conservation of mechanical energy.

Dynamics of particle systems. Linear momentum of a particle system. Conservation of linear momentum of a particle system. Center of mass of a particle system. Decomposition of the dynamics of a particle system. Kinetic energy and work in a particle system. Conservation of energy of a particle system. Collisions.

Rigid body dynamics. Kinematics of rigid body rotation. Rotational kinetic energy of a rigid body. Moment of inertia. Steiner's theorem. Perpendicular axes theorem. Moment of a force. Angular momentum of a rigid body. Principal axes of inertia of a rigid body. Fundamental equation of rigid body rotational dynamics. Rolling motion of a rigid body.
Rigid body statics. Equilibrium conditions of a rigid body. Couple of forces. Constraint forces in mechanical systems. Reactions at support points and connections. Center of gravity.
Experimental study of uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion.
Simple pendulum. Experimental determination of gravity.
Experimental determination of the elastic constant of a spring.
Atwood machine. Experimental determination of an unknown mass.
Experimental determination of the moment of inertia of a disk.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, the final overall grade must be equal to or greater than 50% (5 out of 10). Additionally, the minimum grade for the final written exam must be equal to or greater than 2.4 out of 6. If the student does not achieve 2.4 out of 6 in the final written exam, the final course grade will be FAIL, with the numerical grade resulting from the weighted sum of the grades obtained, truncated to a maximum of 4 points out of 10. In case of plagiarism and/or fraudulent execution, that activity/test will be graded with zero, and the course will be graded as FAIL with a numerical grade that cannot exceed 3 in the examination period in which the fraud occurred.
